title: Bleaching a population of C. elegans nematode worm in a tube
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5ucg6sw

steps.title: Harvest worms into M9
steps.instruction: Wash gravid‑hermaphrodite plates with M9, collect the suspension in a 15 mL Falcon tube and bring the volume to 14 mL M9.

substeps.instruction: Pipet M9 across the plate several times to loosen worms and eggs.
Collect the M9‑worm suspension in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Top up to a final volume of 14 mL M9.
Tip: To prevent adult hermaphrodites sticking to plastic pipettes, add NP40 0.005 % or Tween to the M9, pre‑wet the pipette in M9 + detergent, or use glass pipettes.
Tip: Pipette gently to avoid pulling agar fragments.

steps.title: Wash worm suspension
steps.instruction: Wash the worm suspension three times (or until clear) with 14 mL M9 by centrifuging, discarding supernatant, and resuspending; after the final wash do not resuspend.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2,000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatant with a vacuum pump.
Resuspend the pellet in 14 mL M9.
Repeat the wash two more times (total three washes).
After the last wash, leave the pellet undisturbed.

steps.title: Add bleaching solution
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of standard bleaching solution to the worm pellet (increase to 6 mL if needed) and, optionally, use a stronger mix of 3 mL 10 M NaOH, 7.5 mL bleach, and 40 mL H₂O.

substeps.instruction: Standard: 5 mL bleaching solution.
Optional: increase to 6 mL for higher worm numbers or contamination.
Optional stronger solution: 3 mL NaOH (10 M) + 7.5 mL bleach + 40 mL H₂O.

steps.title: Bleach by vortexing
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube for 6 minutes, then examine under a dissecting microscope; if worms are not fully dissolved, vortex up to 2 additional minutes but avoid over‑bleaching.

substeps.instruction: Vortex for 6 minutes.
Check under a dissecting microscope through the tube; only eggs should remain.
If necessary, vortex an additional 2 minutes (do not exceed).

steps.title: Dilute and pellet eggs
steps.instruction: Add sterile M9 to bring the total volume to ≤14 mL, spin 1 minute at 2,000 rpm, and discard the supernatant with a vacuum pump.

substeps.instruction: Add sterile M9 up to a final volume of 14 mL.
Centrifuge 1 minute at 2,000 rpm.
Discard supernatant using a vacuum pump.

steps.title: Wash eggs three times
steps.instruction: Resuspend the egg pellet in 14 mL sterile M9, vortex 5 seconds while holding the tube horizontally, spin 1 minute at 2,000 rpm, discard supernatant, and repeat this wash three times.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 14 mL sterile M9.
Vortex for 5 seconds, tube held horizontally.
Centrifuge 1 minute at 2,000 rpm.
Discard supernatant with vacuum pump.
Repeat the entire wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Final resuspension and synchronization
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final egg pellet in the desired volume; either pipette onto an NGM plate using a glass pipette or keep in ~4 mL sterile M9 on a rotating wheel at 20 °C overnight to obtain synchronized L1 larvae the next day.

substeps.instruction: Option A: Pipette eggs onto an NGM plate (use a glass pipette).
Option B: Leave eggs in ~4 mL sterile M9, place tube on a rotating wheel at 20 °C overnight.
